findings.issue: Production deploy workflow has no staging environment or canary step — deploys directly to production droplet with zero traffic splitting or rollback capability
findings.impact: Any bad deploy immediately affects all production users. No gradual rollout, no health check before full traffic cutover. Rollback requires a second deploy.
findings.fix: Add a blue/green deployment strategy or at minimum: (1) deploy to staging compose, (2) health check, (3) swap Caddy upstream to new containers, (4) hold old containers for rollback window

findings.issue: Production deploy uses ssh-keyscan with no strict host key checking — `StrictHostKeyChecking=no` accepts any host key
findings.impact: Man-in-the-middle attack on SSH deploy connections. The deploy script connects to the production droplet without verifying its host key.
findings.fix: Add known_hosts entry for the production droplet IP/hostname. Use StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new as minimum.

findings.issue: Production compose uses `image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/api:latest` tag — ':latest' is mutable and can be overwritten by a failed build
findings.impact: A partially built or broken image can replace the ':latest' tag, breaking future rollouts. No way to know which exact SHA is running in production.
findings.fix: Use immutable tags: SHA-based (api:sha-abc123) or build-number-based. Update deploy workflow to reference the specific tag.

findings.issue: Production deploy workflow uses `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` secrets for Terraform remote state — these are also used in infra-development.yml which provisions the infrastructure
findings.impact: Secrets are shared across workflows with no scoping. The production deploy workflow doesn't need Terraform state access — it deploys code, not infra.
findings.fix: Remove Terraform state secrets from deploy-production.yml. Use separate read-only deploy tokens if infra state lookup is needed.

findings.issue: Production web service has no CPU/memory resource limits set — a memory leak in Next.js can OOM the entire droplet
findings.impact: No resource isolation between services. A single runaway container can crash all services on the droplet.
findings.fix: Add deploy.resources.limits block to each service in docker-compose.prod.yml (api: 512MB RAM, web: 512MB RAM, worker: 256MB RAM)

findings.issue: Production compose mounts /var/run/docker.sock for the caddy service with read-write access — Caddy can manage Docker containers
findings.impact: If Caddy is compromised, the attacker has full Docker control. Caddy only needs TLS cert persistence, not Docker socket access.
findings.fix: Remove docker socket mount. Caddy TLS certs should be stored in a named volume instead.

findings.issue: Dev deploy workflow has `--force-recreate` flag but no `--pull always` — containers use the local cached image even if a newer version exists in GHCR
findings.impact: Deploy may use stale images if the build step was skipped or failed. Not pulling means the running image can diverge from the registry.
findings.fix: Add `--pull always` to docker compose up in deploy-development.yml

findings.issue: Production deploy runbook is incomplete — it documents steps 1-3 (build, transfer, compose up) but has no section for rollback, no section for monitoring the deploy, no section for verifying the deploy succeeded
findings.impact: Operators following the runbook during an incident will have incomplete guidance. Missing critical out-of-band steps.
findings.fix: Add rollback procedure, post-deploy verification checklist, and monitoring dashboard links to the runbook.
